dedupe_keys.name: allision risk between large ships and us bridges

description: Allision Risk between Large Ships and US Bridges is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Michael Shields, Johns Hopkins University (jhu.edu). This project contains scripts and data used for a large vessel allision vulnerability assessment of all bridges across the United States. We were motivated by the collapse of the Francis Scott Key Bridge, and implemented the vulnerability assessment methodology prescribed by the American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (Method II). Coverage: Baltimore Maryland, United States. DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 5 top-level files (MD). Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-ytp7-5s85. Keywords: US bridges, large ships, allision risk, vulnerability assessment, risk assessment, Man-Made Hazard. Published 2026-08-24. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
